The whispers draw me deeper in. Warm, gentle, like a mother comforting her cub. An old friend welcoming me home. Is this my home now? They remind me I'm still alive, still hungry. Always so hungry. I'm disgusting.

I ended a life today. A Vigil patrol. Norn. I don't know why I did it, but it felt wonderful. The whispering friend told me I was doing so well. And as the light drained from his eyes, my stomach growled. My body acted without thinking, and before I knew it, he was gone. I'm vile.

What am I becoming? Is it a trick of the light on the snow, or do my claws grow longer? Why does the hunger gnaw away even now, after I did this horrible thing? What's wrong with me? Koda, help me.

While I can see the cruelty behind using chak as a resource, the advancements they've been able to make here *should* benefit, *could* benefit, so many people. I can't expose my bias, though. The Inquest is still a thing, and if any of this is going to fall apart it might as well start with them. It always does, after all. It's just disappointing to live in a world where something that can benefit a lot of people can cause harm... But maybe I'm being naive. That's just how the world works, right? Feeling my morality a bit, is all...  

The Rata Novans seem to have things under control, but for how much longer? We haven't seen how the Kryptis will affect this place, yet, but I can't imagine it going well. It never does.  

After we wrap things up here for the day, Dagda is taking me with her to the observatory. Another fractal, tucked away in the islands. Apparently she and Waiting Sorrow used it as research facility... I'm just happy Dagda is bringing me along. I'm feeling more helpful now than I have in years. Like I'm a part of something bigger than me, which would have threatened me years ago. But, now... It's different.

It's been a relief to have something to keep track of tales and songs I've heard over the years. Easier to recite or riff on their original lines than to trust it to memory all the time, not to mention working on my own original pieces. 

--- 

From Orrian shores to Maguuma's coast,  
Down fiery path and saga of frost,  
O'er seas of jade at world's unend,  
A cycle reborn, a world to mend.  

*Notes: It's fine, but the connection to the Second Scion isn't as strong as I'd like. Maybe someone closer to Aurene can get it right?*

--- 

~~Her~~ fangs ~~were~~ out, ~~her~~ blade ~~was~~ sharp  
Vengeance stirred within her heart  
Oaths and lessons, never forsaken  
~~The Soulkeeper's~~ Her Vigil ~~forever~~ unshaken  

*Notes: I picked this one up while visiting a friend at Vigil Keep. One of the norn warmasters was rather passionately reciting it from the commissary. From what I've heard, the lyrics of the original song were shorter and punchier, so I've cut back some the excess to honor the original form.* 

--- 

Alas poor Dougal, down on his luck.  
An ancient charr relic, a deal was struck.  
Friends and foes fell, an ally's oath spurned.  
Claw in Keane hands, the addled king yearned.  
Peace forged of doom, its ember yet burns.  

*Notes: This one may be my favorite. It could be abbreviated further, but sometimes it's nice to let a tale flourish a little extra. Funny enough, I heard this one most in Ascalon. I wonder if Dougal knows that hulking feline soldiers and engineers gleefully chant his daring deeds?* 

--- 

Scholarly Firstborn, a burden he bore.  
Three factions rallied—a Pact bound for Orr.  
Armed with insight and Riannoc's blade.  
To artesian waters his Wyld Hunt bade.  
Life blooms anew, a legacy made.  

*Notes: Trahearne's passing came as a blow to us, following the terrors of Mordremoth. I was heartened to hear many tales of him afterward that focused on his greatest triumph rather than the tragedy that befell him.* 

--- 

"That's my cue!" the mad sylvari cooed.   
With clockwork knights she struck,  
Those on her list. What luck!  
"Begone you little pest," she said.  
"Desist, my dears, or you'll be dead."  

*Notes: I admit, I was baffled to hear that something had been written about Scarlet Briar, of all people. Some dubious bard in Divinity's Reach must have appreciated her flair for the dramatic? I guess if there were any Secondborn to write about, she'd be the one.* 

--- 

~~Gathering~~ Council held, ~~in~~ times most dire.  
Subtle as shadow, tempting ~~their~~ ire.  
~~A~~ Barrier ~~she~~ raised, against Mantle plot  
~~To claim~~ For Kryta's throne, ~~but all was for naught.~~  
~~Her allies struck true.~~ May Caudecus rot!  

*Notes: Picked this one up in the promenade outside the queen's palace. I've made some revisions of my own, but I feel like someone who knows Her Majesty could punch this up just a bit more and give it a personal touch.* 

*Still, it would be an honor to perform this for her one day. Think of the exposure!*

The situation in the Kryta fractal has developed in an unanticipated direction. While the emergence of Thackeray as the nation's leader after the deaths of the royal family was unsurprising, the deterioration of Krytan society was unexpected.
